history.idea:
Replace the random order with a filter-and-dedupe pipeline that keeps only clean, target-style (WikiText-like) documents.

1. Dedupe: drop exact duplicates by hash of whitespace-normalised text, and near-duplicates by hash of the first 300 characters. Keep the first occurrence.

2. Damage filter: drop docs under 200 characters. Drop docs where more than 0.5% of alphabetic words mix Latin letters with Cyrillic, Armenian or Greek letters (homoglyph damage).

3. Word-order and domain score: lowercase and whitespace-tokenise. Build the set of word bigrams from the 200 target_sample docs. For each pool doc, compute h = the fraction of its first 600 word bigrams that are in that set. Calibrate the threshold by leave-out: split target_sample 100/100, build the bigram set from one half, compute h on the other half, and scale for the smaller set by doing it both ways. Set the threshold to about 0.75 times the 5th percentile of the held-out target h. Drop docs below it. This removes word-shuffled articles (correct unigrams, broken bigrams) and the spam and web text.

4. Style score: require WikiText formatting. The doc must start with "= " or have a spaced-punctuation rate (count of " , ", " . " and " @-@ " per word) of at least half the target sample's 5th percentile.

5. Output: return only the surviving docs, shuffled with random.Random(CURATE_SEED). If they total fewer than T tokens, let the trainer cycle them and add no filler. Estimate tokens as len(text)/4 to stay fast.
history.outcome: dev 1.8842 against 1.9643 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea: Score the whole document for damage instead of only its head. Keep the pipeline, shuffle and no-filler behaviour unchanged, and change only the bigram filter. (1) Split each pool doc's lowercased whitespace tokens into consecutive windows of 300 word bigrams, merging a final window shorter than 100 into the previous one, and compute the target-bigram hit fraction per window against full_set. (2) Calibrate the same way on the 100/100 target halves: collect per-window held-out hit fractions and set w_thresh = 0.75 x their 2nd percentile. (3) Drop a doc if its mean window score is below the existing h_thresh, or if more than 10% of its windows (and at least one) fall below w_thresh. (4) Add a character check: build the set of characters that occur in target_sample, and drop docs where more than 1% of characters are outside that set. Log the number of docs kept and their estimated tokens.
history.outcome: dev 1.8622 against 1.8842 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea:
Tighten duplicate and residual-damage removal among the survivors; keep the shuffle and no-filler behaviour unchanged.

(1) Best-copy dedupe by title. Run all quality filters first and collect survivors with their mean window score. Group survivors by a title key: the first line, whitespace-normalised and lowercased, if the doc starts with "= "; otherwise the existing first-300-chars key. Keep one doc per group: highest mean bigram window score, ties broken by longer text, then lower index. This replaces "first occurrence wins".

(2) Content near-dup check. For each kept doc, hash every word 8-gram starting at word positions divisible by 50. Process docs in descending mean-score order. Drop a doc if more than 30% of its sampled hashes already appear in previously kept docs.

(3) Case-sensitive word check. Build the case-sensitive whitespace-token vocabulary of target_sample. For each pool doc, compute per 300-token window the fraction of tokens in that vocabulary. Calibrate on the 100/100 target halves as for the bigrams: v_thresh = 0.85 x the 2nd percentile of held-out window fractions. Drop a doc if more than 10% of its windows (and at least one) fall below v_thresh. This catches case-flipped, lowercased or uppercased copies and character-typo noise that the lowercased bigram test lets through.

Log how many docs each of the three steps removes, and the kept token estimate.
history.outcome: dev 1.8623 against 1.8622 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Make the selection budget-aware with exact token counts, keeping all current filters and dedupe unchanged. (1) Count the tokens of each survivor exactly with tiktoken "gpt2" (encode_ordinary_batch, survivors only, to stay inside the time limit) and log the survivor total as a fraction of T. (2) Give each survivor a quality score: its mean bigram window score against full_set (already computed). (3) If the survivors total T tokens or more, sort by quality score, keep the best docs until the cumulative total just reaches T and drop the rest, then shuffle the kept docs with the seed. (4) If the survivors total less than T, do not rely on blind cycling. Return pass 1 as all survivors in seeded shuffle order, followed by a filler pass covering the remaining T minus total tokens. The filler is the highest-scoring survivors, taken in descending score order until the remainder is covered, then shuffled with a second seeded RNG. If the remainder exceeds one full pass, append further full shuffled passes first. (5) In both cases, drop survivors whose distinct word-trigram fraction is below 0.75 times the 2nd percentile of that fraction in target_sample, computed on the first 2000 words. This removes internally repetitive junk that the bigram test passes. Log how many docs each branch and the repetition filter affect.
history.outcome: dev 1.8599 against 1.8622 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Make the bigram filter stricter and calibrate it exactly, changing nothing else (same char, style and homoglyph filters, same dedupe, seeded shuffle, no filler).

(1) Replace the 100/100 half-split calibration with leave-one-out. Compute, for each lowercased word bigram, the number of target_sample docs that contain it (document frequency). When scoring target doc d, a bigram counts as a hit only if it occurs in at least one other target doc (df >= 2, or df == 1 and not from d). This gives each target doc's window scores against a 199-doc set, which matches how pool docs are scored against full_set.

(2) Remove the 0.75 slack. Set h_thresh to the 2nd percentile of the leave-one-out mean window scores of the target docs. Set w_thresh to the 1st percentile of the leave-one-out per-window scores.

(3) Drop a pool doc if its mean window score is below h_thresh, or if more than 5% of its windows (and at least one) are below w_thresh. The current limit is 10%.

(4) Log both thresholds, the number of docs kept, and how many docs pass the old rule but fail the new one.
history.outcome: dev 1.8322 against 1.8622 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

history.idea:
Add two vocabulary-independent word-order checks after the existing bigram rule, to catch shuffled or partly shuffled articles that it still passes. Leave every other filter, the dedupe, the seeded shuffle and the no-filler behaviour unchanged.

(A) Closed-class bigram test.
- Take the 200 most frequent lowercased whitespace tokens of target_sample (function words and punctuation); call this set C.
- Build F = the set of adjacent pairs (a, b), both in C, that occur in at least 2 target docs. This is the same leave-one-out trick as the current rule (df >= 2).
- For each doc, reuse the existing 300-bigram windows. In each window, look only at adjacent pairs with both tokens in C and compute the fraction that are in F. Skip a window with fewer than 30 such pairs.
- Calibrate c_thresh as the 1st percentile of these window scores over the target docs. Pool docs are scored against the set of all target C-pairs (df >= 1), mirroring full_set versus loo_set.
- Drop a pool doc if more than 5% of its scored windows (and at least one) are below c_thresh.

(B) Sentence-start test.
- For each doc, find every " . " token that is followed by another token on the same line.
- Compute the fraction of those where the next token starts with an uppercase letter, a digit, or one of the characters " ' ( = .
- Set s_thresh to 0.95 times the minimum of this fraction over target docs that have at least 10 such positions.
- Drop pool docs with at least 10 such positions whose fraction is below s_thresh.

Log both thresholds, how many survivors of the current filters each test removes, and the kept token estimate.
history.outcome: dev 1.8319 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea: Tighten the existing leave-one-out bigram rule one more notch and change nothing else (same character, style and homoglyph filters, same dedupe, seeded shuffle, no filler). (1) Set H_PERCENTILE = 10, so h_thresh is the 10th percentile of the leave-one-out mean window scores of the target docs (currently the 2nd). (2) Set W_PERCENTILE = 3, so w_thresh is the 3rd percentile of the leave-one-out window scores (currently the 1st). (3) Keep the bad-window limit at 5% for docs with 20 or more windows. For docs with fewer than 20 windows, keep the current behaviour (one window below w_thresh drops the doc). (4) Remove the old-rule comparison code. Instead log how many docs pass the current thresholds (p2/p1) but fail the new ones (p10/p3), split into failures of the mean rule and of the window rule. Also log the kept doc count and the kept token estimate as a fraction of T.
history.outcome: dev 1.8355 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Add a second, self-trained pass that rescues clean target-style docs the bigram rule currently rejects. Keep every existing filter, the dedupe, the seeded shuffle and the no-filler behaviour.

Stage 1 (unchanged): run the current pipeline and call its output the survivors. All survivors stay in the output.

Stage 2 (new):
(1) Build a reference set R2 of lowercased word bigrams from all survivors plus all 200 target docs. Use the same tokenisation as now.
(2) Calibrate on target_sample, whose docs are not in the pool. Score each target doc with the existing 300-bigram windows against the survivor-only bigram set. Set h2 to the 2nd percentile of the per-doc mean window scores and w2 to the 1st percentile of all window scores, with no slack.
(3) Take as candidates every pool doc that passed the length, unseen-character, style and homoglyph filters but failed the stage-1 bigram rule. The style and homoglyph checks must therefore be evaluated for rejected docs too.
(4) Score each candidate's windows against R2. Rescue it if its mean is at least h2 and at most 5% of its windows are below w2. As now, a single bad window drops a doc with fewer than 20 windows.
(5) Guard against damaged copies of survivors, whose scores are inflated by their clean twin. Do not rescue a candidate whose whitespace-normalised, lowercased first line equals the first line of any survivor or of an already rescued doc. Also apply the existing exact and first-300-character dedupe keys against the survivors.
(6) Append the rescued docs to the survivors, then do the single seeded shuffle.

Log h2, w2, the number of candidates, the number rescued, the number blocked by the title guard, and the kept token estimate before and after. Keep runtime in budget by building R2 once as a Python set of bigram tuples, or of 64-bit hashes if memory is tight.
history.outcome: dev 1.8258 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Extend the rescue pass of experiment 8 (the lowest dev so far, 1.8258) into an iterated self-training loop with a stronger twin guard. Keep stage 1 (the current pipeline) unchanged, keep the seeded shuffle and add no filler.

(1) Stage 1: run the current filters and dedupe; the output is the survivors. Also evaluate the length, unseen-character, style and homoglyph filters for docs that fail the bigram rule. Those that pass are the candidates.

(2) Reference set: build R as a Python set of 64-bit ints, hash((a, b)), of the lowercased word bigrams of all survivors plus the 200 target docs.

(3) Calibration, done once: score the target docs with the existing 300-bigram windows against the survivor-only bigram set. Set h2 to the 2nd percentile of the per-doc means and w2 to the 1st percentile of all window scores, with no slack.

(4) Twin guard: build G, a set of hashes of lowercased word 6-grams of the survivors, keeping only 6-grams with hash % 8 == 0 (content-defined sampling). Block a candidate if
- more than 15% of its own sampled 6-grams (at least 5 sampled) are in G, or
- its whitespace-normalised, lowercased first line equals that of a kept doc, or
- it matches the existing exact or first-300-character dedupe keys.

(5) Rounds, at most 3, stopping early if a round rescues fewer than 20 docs: score each remaining, unblocked candidate against R. Rescue it if its mean is at least h2 and at most 5% of its windows are below w2 (a single bad window drops a doc with fewer than 20 windows). Process candidates in descending mean order. After each rescue, add the doc's title, dedupe keys and sampled 6-grams to the guards immediately, so that a twin later in the same round is blocked. Add the bigrams of the rescued docs to R only at the end of the round.

(6) Output: survivors plus all rescued docs, in one seeded shuffle.

Log h2, w2, the candidate count, the number rescued per round, the number blocked by each guard, and the kept token estimate as a fraction of T before and after.
history.outcome: dev 1.8300 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Add a self-trained re-scoring stage that both purges and rescues, using the stage-1 survivors as a much larger reference than the 200 target docs. Keep stage 1, the seeded shuffle and the no-filler behaviour unchanged.

(1) Stage 1: run the current pipeline to get survivors S. Also evaluate the length, unseen-character, style and homoglyph filters for docs that fail the bigram rule. Those that pass are candidates C.

(2) Reference: over S, compute document frequency (count each doc once) of
- lowercased word bigrams -> df_bg, stored as a dict keyed by hash((a, b)) to save memory;
- case-sensitive whitespace tokens -> df_tok.

(3) Scoring, with the existing 300-bigram windows. A bigram or token is a hit if its df, excluding the scored doc's own contribution, is at least 2. So for a doc in S the test is df >= 3, and for a candidate or a target doc it is df >= 2. This makes target docs (not in the pool) and pool docs comparable, and stops one damaged twin from validating a doc. Compute per window:
- b = bigram hit fraction;
- v = token hit fraction (case-sensitive).

(4) Calibrate on target_sample scored the same way, with no slack: hb = 2nd percentile of per-doc mean b; wb = 1st percentile of window b; wv = 1st percentile of window v.

(5) Final keep rule for every doc in S and C: mean b >= hb, and at most 5% of windows (a single one for docs with fewer than 20 windows) have b < wb or v < wv.
- S docs that fail are purged. This targets residual light typo, case or local-shuffle damage that the coarse 200-doc reference cannot resolve.
- C docs that pass are rescued, subject to the existing exact and first-300-character dedupe keys and a guard that the lowercased first line does not equal that of any kept doc.

(6) Output the kept S docs plus the rescued docs in one seeded shuffle.

Log hb, wb, wv, the number purged (split by b rule and v rule), the number rescued, the number blocked by the guards, and the kept token estimate before and after.
history.outcome: dev 1.8334 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Combine the two rejected changes that each lowered dev (experiment 8's rescue pass, 1.8258, and experiment 4's exact token budgeting, 1.8599) into one pipeline. Keep stage 1 (all current filters, thresholds and dedupe) unchanged.

(1) Stage 1: run the current pipeline to get the survivors, each with its mean window score against full_set. Also evaluate the length, unseen-character, style and homoglyph filters for docs that fail the bigram rule; those that pass are the candidates.

(2) Rescue, exactly as in experiment 8:
- Build R2, the set of lowercased word bigrams of all survivors plus the 200 target docs (store 64-bit hashes if memory is tight).
- Calibrate by scoring the target docs with the existing 300-bigram windows against the survivor-only bigram set: h2 = 2nd percentile of per-doc means, w2 = 1st percentile of all window scores, no slack.
- Rescue a candidate if its mean against R2 is at least h2 and at most 5% of its windows are below w2 (a single bad window drops a doc with fewer than 20 windows).
- Do not rescue a candidate whose whitespace-normalised, lowercased first line equals that of a survivor or an already rescued doc, or which matches the existing exact or first-300-character dedupe keys.

(3) Exact budget: count the tokens of every kept doc (survivors plus rescued) with tiktoken "gpt2" encode_ordinary_batch. Give each doc a quality score: its percentile rank of mean window score within its own group (survivors against full_set, rescued against R2), with every rescued doc ranked below every survivor.

(4a) If the kept total is at least T: drop the lowest-quality docs (rescued first) until the total just covers T, then do one seeded shuffle.

(4b) If the kept total is below T: do not rely on blind cycling. Output pass 1 as all kept docs in seeded shuffle order. Then add a filler pass covering exactly the remaining T minus total tokens, made of the highest-quality survivors (never rescued docs) in descending quality until the remainder is covered, shuffled with a second RNG seeded CURATE_SEED+1. If the remainder exceeds one full pass, insert further full shuffled passes before the filler.

Log h2, w2, the candidate count, the number rescued, the number blocked by the guards, the exact kept tokens as a fraction of T before and after rescue, and which branch (4a or 4b) ran with the number of docs dropped or repeated.
history.outcome: dev 1.8378 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected

history.idea:
Fix the small-document false-rejection in the window rule, and change nothing else (same character, style and homoglyph filters, same h_thresh mean rule, same dedupe, seeded shuffle, no filler).

Problem: w_thresh is the 1st percentile of leave-one-out target windows, so about 1% of clean windows fall below it. A doc with fewer than 20 windows is dropped by a single such window, so a clean 10-19 window article is falsely rejected roughly 10-17% of the time. These are the longest clean articles.

Change:
(1) Add a hard floor: w_floor = the minimum leave-one-out window score over all target docs (the same loo_windows list already computed).
(2) Count n_bad = windows below w_thresh, and n_very_bad = windows below w_floor.
(3) New window rule. Drop the doc if any of these holds:
- n_very_bad >= 1 (a window worse than anything seen in clean target text);
- n_bad >= 2 and n_bad > 5% of the windows;
- n_bad == 1 and the doc has fewer than 4 windows (short docs keep the current strict behaviour, since one window is a large share of them).
Otherwise keep it. So a doc with 4 or more windows may have one mildly low window (between w_floor and w_thresh); the 5% limit applies as before to docs with 20 or more windows.
(4) Keep the mean rule (mean >= h_thresh, 2nd percentile) exactly as now.
(5) Remove the old-rule comparison code. Log w_floor, the number of docs newly admitted by this change (pass new rule, fail current rule) with their estimated tokens, and the kept token estimate as a fraction of T before and after.
history.outcome: dev 1.8241 against 1.8322 for the best at the time, rejected
